# ieeeck

> Checks whether infinity and NaN arithmetic is safe.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ieeeck from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ieeeck';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ieeeck( ispec, zero, one ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ispec` | `integer` | in |  |  | `0` checks infinity arithmetic only; any other value also checks NaN arithmetic |
| `zero` | `number` | in |  |  | the value `0.0` |
| `one` | `number` | in |  |  | the value `1.0` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ispec`: Specifies whether to test just for infinity arithmetic or whether to test for infinity and NaN arithmetic.

  -   `= 0`: Verify infinity arithmetic only.
  -   `= 1`: Verify infinity and NaN arithmetic.
- `zero`: Must contain the value 0.0 This is passed to prevent the compiler from optimizing away this code.
- `one`: Must contain the value 1.0 This is passed to prevent the compiler from optimizing away this code.

  RETURN VALUE: INTEGER

  -   = 0: Arithmetic failed to produce the correct answers
  -   = 1: Arithmetic produced the correct answers

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `1` if the arithmetic is safe, `0` otherwise

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ieeeck.ndarray( ispec, zero, one ) → integer
```

Checks whether infinity and NaN arithmetic is safe, using alternative indexing semantics (the routine takes no arrays).

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ispec` | `integer` | in |  |  | `0` checks infinity arithmetic only; any other value also checks NaN arithmetic |
| `zero` | `number` | in |  |  | the value `0.0` |
| `one` | `number` | in |  |  | the value `1.0` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ispec`: Specifies whether to test just for infinity arithmetic or whether to test for infinity and NaN arithmetic.

  -   `= 0`: Verify infinity arithmetic only.
  -   `= 1`: Verify infinity and NaN arithmetic.
- `zero`: Must contain the value 0.0 This is passed to prevent the compiler from optimizing away this code.
- `one`: Must contain the value 1.0 This is passed to prevent the compiler from optimizing away this code.

  RETURN VALUE: INTEGER

  -   = 0: Arithmetic failed to produce the correct answers
  -   = 1: Arithmetic produced the correct answers

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `1` if the arithmetic is safe, `0` otherwise

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `ieeeck()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`IEEECK`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/ieeeck.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import ieeeck from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ieeeck';

console.log( ieeeck( 1, 0.0, 1.0 ) );
// => 1

console.log( ieeeck.ndarray( 1, 0.0, 1.0 ) );
// => 1
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `IEEECK`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

IEEECK is called from the ILAENV to verify that Infinity and possibly NaN arithmetic is safe (i.e. will not trap).

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
